findings.title: One accessible message, differentiated address
findings.claim: The revelation made accessible in the Messenger's language carries glad tidings to the God-conscious and warning to an obstinate people; wider recurrences show this shared address meeting differentiated reception.
findings.mechanism: In 19:97 the same revelation is the object of ease through the Messenger's tongue and the repeated means بِهِ for both glad tidings and warning. The wider 44:58 repeats the ease-in-your-tongue wording for remembrance, and 46:12 joins an Arabic confirming Book with warning for wrongdoers and glad tidings for doers of good. These contacts make the focus's paired purposes legible as a recurring pattern in how the revealed message reaches different audiences. At 2:204, the phrase أَلَدُّ ٱلْخِصَامِ gives a wider contention image that returns through لُّدًّا and sharpens the warned group's characterization.
findings.reader_payoff: The reader can see one accessible message serving two recipient-directed acts, while the contentiousness of the warned group and the difference in reception gain wider textual context.
findings.containment: The focus keeps its plain scene intact: the Messenger is enabled to announce glad tidings to the God-conscious and warn an obstinate group. The wider parallels illuminate recurrence; they do not establish quotation, identical audiences, or a claim that ease guarantees a particular response. The l-d-d characterization remains bounded to the focus's named group.

epistemic.reason: The cross-run support is trusted, and the cited target Arabic supplies concrete wider contacts. The l-s-n branch is marked qualified, and connection records do not supply target morphology, so the cross-ayah pattern is retained with that limitation explicit.

branch_activations.branch_gloss: sevindirici haber verme; kötü haberde açık nitelemeli alaycı bildirim
branch_activations.facet_statement: Bir kişiye onu sevindirecek bir haber verilir.
branch_activations.carrier: تُبَشِّرَ carries the ordinary act of giving glad tidings to a recipient.
branch_activations.independent_trigger: The supplied Arabic of 46:12 presents an Arabic confirming Book with glad tidings for the doers of good alongside warning for wrongdoers.
branch_activations.activation: The wider Book's glad-tidings clause meets the focus verb تُبَشِّرَ through the same message-and-recipient relation; returning to 19:97, the verse's good-news act belongs to a broader paired address.
branch_activations.resulting_reading: Glad tidings in the focus participate in a recurring Qur'anic pattern in which the revealed message addresses a receptive class with good news.
branch_activations.boundary: The focus's recipient remains al-muttaqīn; 46:12 does not make the two recipient groups identical or change the ordinary good-news sense.

branch_activations.facet_statement: Çekirdek, hasımlıkta gösterilen olağandan güçlü, inatçı ve dirençli çekişmedir.
branch_activations.carrier: لُّدًّا characterizes the warned people as intensely stubborn and contentious.
branch_activations.independent_trigger: The supplied Arabic of 2:204 describes أَلَدُّ ٱلْخِصَامِ, intensely contentious disputation.
branch_activations.activation: The wider contentious-disputation image meets the focus adjective لُّدًّا and its supplied core of resistant contention, so the warning's audience is heard as actively disputatious rather than merely unnamed.
branch_activations.resulting_reading: The warned group carries a quality of stubborn, resistant contention that is also visible in a wider Qur'anic description of disputation.
branch_activations.boundary: The focus adjective remains a characterization of its own warned group; the person and surrounding conflict in 2:204 are not transferred to 19:97.

branch_activations.facet_statement: Bir topluluğun kullandığı dil sistemi ve o sistemle gerçekleşen konuşmadır.
branch_activations.carrier: لِسَانِكَ names the addressed tongue-language as the medium through which the revelation is made accessible.
branch_activations.independent_trigger: The supplied Arabic of 44:58 repeats the wording بِلِسَانِكَ in the statement that the message is made easy in the Messenger's tongue for remembrance.
branch_activations.activation: The repeated tongue-language phrase contacts لِسَانِكَ in the focus, making its language-medium reading recur in a wider Quranic setting and linking that medium to the two purposes that follow here.
branch_activations.resulting_reading: The focus's personalized language-medium is part of a recurring account of the Quran's accessible delivery.
branch_activations.boundary: The language branch is marked qualified and the connection packet does not provide target morphology; this recurrence does not claim that language is the only medium of the revelation.

branch_activations.facet_statement: Bir kişi ya da topluluğa korkulacak bir durumu haber vererek onları sakınmaya yöneltir.
branch_activations.carrier: تُنذِرَ carries the act of warning a people by reporting what they should fear.
branch_activations.independent_trigger: The supplied Arabic of 46:12 says the Arabic confirming Book warns those who do wrong, in the same passage that gives glad tidings to doers of good.
branch_activations.activation: The wider warning clause meets the focus's warning verb and the same message-and-recipient structure; on return, the paired good-news and warning purposes are part of a recurring account of revelation's address.
branch_activations.resulting_reading: Warning in 19:97 is one side of a repeated Qur'anic pattern where the revealed message addresses wrongdoers as well as doers of good.
branch_activations.boundary: The focus still addresses qawman luddan; 46:12 does not identify those groups or supply the focus's particular warning content.

branch_activations.facet_statement: Temel anlam, güç ve çetin olanın karşıtı biçimindeki kolaylıktır.
branch_activations.carrier: يَسَّرْنَٰهُ carries the caused facilitation of the revelation.
branch_activations.independent_trigger: The supplied Arabic of 44:58 repeats the focus wording yassarnāhu bi-lisānika and names remembrance as its purpose.
branch_activations.activation: The repeated ease-in-the-Messenger's-language formula meets the focus verb in a wider ayah; the focus then specifies two recipient-directed purposes for this accessible message.
branch_activations.resulting_reading: The focus's facilitation joins a recurring Quranic description of accessible delivery, here serving glad tidings and warning.
branch_activations.boundary: The recurrence does not make the purposes in both ayat identical or imply that facilitation determines how every hearer responds.
